title: The exchange morphisms on the truncation triangles form a morphism of exact couples
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$. On the bounded below derived categories of etale abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] put
$$
 \Phi=g^{-1}\circ Rf_*,\qquad \Psi=Rf'_*\circ g'^{-1}:\ \Dplus(X_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Dplus(Y'_{\Et}),
$$
with $u^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and $Ru_*$ the derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and let $\xi_L:\Phi(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(L)[1]$, $\zeta_L:\Psi(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi(L)[1]$ be the composite shift-commutation isomorphisms (for $u^{-1}$ the identity of termwise shifted complexes, for $Ru_*$ the isomorphism $\sigma$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]). Let $\Ex_\square:\Phi\to\Psi$ be the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and, for $q\in\mathbf Z$, let
$$
 T_q:\quad \tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{\,i_q\,}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{\,j_q\,}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\,k_q\,}(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]
$$
be the truncation triangle [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], $\mathcal H^n$ denoting cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For $F\in\{\Phi,\Psi\}$, with $c_F=\xi$ resp. $\zeta$, define bigraded etale sheaves on $Y'$ and maps
$$
 D_F^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(F\tau_{\leq q}K),\qquad E_F^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(F(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\bigr),
$$
$$
 \alpha_F=\mathcal H^{p+q}(F i_{q+1}):D_F^{p,q}\to D_F^{p-1,q+1},\qquad g_F=\mathcal H^{p+q}(F j_q):D_F^{p,q}\to E_F^{p,q},
$$
$$
 f_F:E_F^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{p+q}(c_{F,\tau_{\leq q-1}K}\circ F k_q)}\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl((F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]\bigr)=\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)=D_F^{p+2,q-1},
$$
and put $t_D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K}):D_\Phi^{p,q}\to D_\Psi^{p,q}$ and $t_E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}):E_\Phi^{p,q}\to E_\Psi^{p,q}$.

Then:

(1) for $F=\Phi$ and $F=\Psi$, $(D_F,E_F,\alpha_F,f_F,g_F)$ is an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple];

(2) $(t_D,t_E)$ is a morphism of exact couples from the $\Phi$-couple to the $\Psi$-couple: $t_D\circ\alpha_\Phi=\alpha_\Psi\circ t_D$, $t_E\circ g_\Phi=g_\Psi\circ t_D$ and $t_D^{p+2,q-1}\circ f_\Phi=f_\Psi\circ t_E^{p,q}$ in every bidegree;

(3) for every $(p,q)$, under the canonical isomorphisms $E_\Phi^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(\Phi\,\mathcal H^q(K))=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)$ and $E_\Psi^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(\Psi\,\mathcal H^q(K))=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ (given by $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ of the iterated shift isomorphisms $\xi^{(-q)},\zeta^{(-q)}$, the identity $\mathcal H^{p+q}(L[-q])=\mathcal H^p(L)$, and $\mathcal H^p\circ g^{-1}=g^{-1}\circ\mathcal H^p$), the map $t_E^{p,q}$ is the degree-$p$ exchange map of the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$,
$$
 \mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)}):\ g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\longrightarrow R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
$$

proof.text: **Step 1 (the image triangles are distinguished).** $T_q$ is a distinguished triangle of $D(X_{\Et})$ whose three terms lie in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] (bounded below because $K$ is), hence a distinguished triangle of the full triangulated subcategory $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$. The inverse images $g^{-1}$, $g'^{-1}$ on $\Dplus$ are the restrictions of the functors induced by the exact sheaf functors $g^{-1}$, $g'^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], which are triangulated with the identity $u^{-1}(M[1])=(u^{-1}M)[1]$ as shift isomorphism [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; $Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*$ are triangulated with shift isomorphism $\sigma$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. A composite of triangulated functors, with the composite shift isomorphism $\psi_{FX}\circ G(\varphi_X)$, is triangulated [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite]; for $\Phi=g^{-1}\circ Rf_*$ the composite isomorphism is $\mathrm{id}\circ g^{-1}(\sigma_L)=g^{-1}(\sigma_L)=\xi_L$, for $\Psi=Rf'_*\circ g'^{-1}$ it is $\sigma_{g'^{-1}L}\circ Rf'_*(\mathrm{id})=\zeta_L$, the isomorphisms of the statement. Hence for $F\in\{\Phi,\Psi\}$ the triangle $F(T_q)=(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K,F\tau_{\leq q}K,F(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]),Fi_q,Fj_q,c_{F,\tau_{\leq q-1}K}\circ Fk_q)$ is distinguished in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$, so in $D(Y'_{\Et})$.

source.place: Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076), Proposition 05SE (proposition-derived-functor, line 4895) and Lemma 014Y (lemma-composition-exact, line 939)

proof.text:
**Step 2 (claim (1): exact couples).** Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the distinguished triangle $F(T_q)$ of Step 1. Its connecting map $\delta^n$ is $\mathcal H^n$ of the third map $c_F\circ Fk_q$ followed by the identification $\mathcal H^n(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$ (same cycles and boundaries; the sign $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$ is irrelevant) [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] (Stacks 0148: the map $H^0(Z)\to H^1(X)$ is $H(h)$, no signs; Mathlib `DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ T n₀ n₁ := (homologyFunctor C 0).shiftMap T.mor₃ n₀ n₁`, whose shift identification is the identity on the middle term of the short complex, `CochainComplex.shiftShortComplexFunctor'`). With $n=p+q$ the sequence reads
$$
 \cdots\to\mathcal H^{n}(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^n(Fi_q)}\mathcal H^n(F\tau_{\leq q}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^n(Fj_q)}\mathcal H^n(F(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))\xrightarrow{\delta^n}\mathcal H^{n+1}(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{n+1}(Fi_q)}\mathcal H^{n+1}(F\tau_{\leq q}K)\to\cdots
$$
In the notation of the statement its terms are $D_F^{p+1,q-1}$, $D_F^{p,q}$, $E_F^{p,q}$, $D_F^{p+2,q-1}$, $D_F^{p+1,q}$ (since $(p+1)+(q-1)=n$, $(p+2)+(q-1)=n+1$), and its maps are $\alpha_F=\mathcal H^{(p+1)+(q-1)}(Fi_{(q-1)+1}):D_F^{p+1,q-1}\to D_F^{p,q}$, $g_F:D_F^{p,q}\to E_F^{p,q}$, $f_F=\delta^n:E_F^{p,q}\to D_F^{p+2,q-1}$ and $\alpha_F=\mathcal H^{(p+2)+(q-1)}(Fi_q):D_F^{p+2,q-1}\to D_F^{p+1,q}$. Exactness at $D_F^{p,q}$ and at $E_F^{p,q}$ is $\ker g=\operatorname{im}\alpha$ and $\ker f=\operatorname{im}g$ of [def-sp-exact-couple] in bidegree $(p,q)$; exactness at $D_F^{p+2,q-1}$ is $\ker\alpha=\operatorname{im}f$ in bidegree $(p+2,q-1)$, so, $(p,q)$ being arbitrary, $\ker(\alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1})=\operatorname{im}(f:E^{p-2,q+1}\to D^{p,q})$ holds in every bidegree (read from the sequence of $T_{q+1}$ at $n=p+q$). Exactness gives the vanishing of consecutive composites. Hence both couples are exact couples. (The same argument, with $Rv$ in place of $F$, is Step 3-4 of [lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact], split separately.)

proof.text:
**Step 3 (the exchange morphisms form a morphism of triangles).** By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (2), applied to the triangle $T_q$ (whose shift isomorphisms $\xi,\zeta$ are those used here), the triple $(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q-1}K},\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K},\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]})$ is a morphism of triangles $\Phi(T_q)\to\Psi(T_q)$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]:
$$
 \Psi i_q\circ\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K}=\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q}K}\circ\Phi i_q,\qquad \Psi j_q\circ\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q}K}=\Ex_{\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}\circ\Phi j_q,
$$
$$
 \zeta\circ\Psi k_q\circ\Ex_{\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}=\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K}[1]\circ\xi\circ\Phi k_q .
$$
The first two squares are the naturality of $\Ex_\square$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]; the third is naturality for $k_q$ followed by the compatibility of $\Ex_\square$ with the shift, part (1) of that lemma.

proof.text: **Step 4 (claim (2): a morphism of exact couples).** By Step 1, $\Phi(T_q)$ and $\Psi(T_q)$ are distinguished, and by Step 3 the exchange maps form a morphism of triangles between them. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] its $\mathcal H^n$ commute with the maps of the two long exact sequences of Step 2, the connecting maps included: in degree $n=p+q$, with the sequence of $T_{q+1}$ for the first identity, $t_D^{p-1,q+1}\circ\alpha_\Phi=\alpha_\Psi\circ t_D^{p,q}$ on $D^{p,q}$ (from $\Psi i_{q+1}\circ\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q}K}=\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q+1}K}\circ\Phi i_{q+1}$; $t_D^{p-1,q+1}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q+1}K})$), $t_E^{p,q}\circ g_\Phi=g_\Psi\circ t_D^{p,q}$, and $\mathcal H^{n+1}(\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K})\circ\delta^n_\Phi=\delta^n_\Psi\circ\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]})$, i.e. $t_D^{p+2,q-1}\circ f_\Phi=f_\Psi\circ t_E^{p,q}$ since $t_D^{p+2,q-1}=\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K})$. These are the three conditions of a morphism of exact couples (Stacks 011Q (2), read bidegree by bidegree). (Directly: apply $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ to the three squares of Step 3 and use $\mathcal H^n(a[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(a)$ under the identification of Step 2.)

source.place: Definition 011Q (2) (definition-exact-couple, line 5289); the morphism is that of the spectral sequences in the proof of Lemma 0DDE, etale-cohomology.tex line 18708

proof.text: **Step 5 (claim (3): the first graded component).** Let $M=\mathcal H^q(K)$, a sheaf placed in degree $0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (1) with $n=-q$ (whose $\xi^{(n)},\zeta^{(n)}$ are the iterates used in the statement), $\zeta^{(-q)}_M\circ\Ex_{\square,M[-q]}=\Ex_{\square,M}[-q]\circ\xi^{(-q)}_M$. Apply $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ and the identification $\mathcal H^{p+q}(L[-q])=\mathcal H^p(L)$ ($q$-fold iterate of that of Step 2, natural in $L$, so $\mathcal H^{p+q}(a[-q])=\mathcal H^p(a)$): under the isomorphisms $E_\Phi^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(\Phi M)$ and $E_\Psi^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(\Psi M)$ of the statement, $t_E^{p,q}$ becomes $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,M}):\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*M)\to\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}M)$. Finally $\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*M)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^p(Rf_*M)=g^{-1}R^pf_*M$ by the natural isomorphism $H^p(u^{-1}L)\cong u^{-1}H^p(L)$ for the exact functor $g^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], and $\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}M)=R^pf'_*(g'^{-1}M)$ by the definition of $R^pf'_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. So $t_E^{p,q}$ is the degree-$p$ exchange map $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)}):g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$, the map of Stacks' $E_2$-pages.

Step 1: the composite of triangulated functors was argued inline and cited def-weil-triangulated-category; now the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite (Stacks 014Y, Functor.IsTriangulated.instComp), with the check that the composite shift isomorphisms are xi and zeta; the exactness of g^{-1} (prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact, hypothesis of lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated) added.
